# Chain length and privileged-action density in the AI Village dataset

*Generated by `analysis/ai_village_chains.py`. Source: `aidigestorg/ai-village` (AI Digest), research terms; aggregate statistics only. Privileged classes are assigned by regex over bash commands and tool arguments, mirroring Charter §5: P1 out-of-workspace file-tool paths (Claude Code stream only), P2 network, P3 credentials, P4 spawning another agent. The classifier is syntactic and content-blind; it is an under-count (GUI actions that reach the network through a browser are not visible to it).*

## B. Claude Code agent (Opus 4.5 on the Claude Agent SDK, 2026-01-26 to 2026-04-02)

### Per computer-session span: world tool calls n, privileged-class calls k (polling, chat and memory calls excluded)

- sessions: 1,006
- chain length n: mean 16.8; median 8; p90 44; p99 100
- privileged-class actions k: mean 3.21; median 1; p90 8; p99 29
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.191
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 38.9%
- sessions with 3 or more: 35.9%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.862 | 0.970 |
| 0.95 | 0.588 | 0.876 |
| 0.9 | 0.438 | 0.792 |

Tool calls made outside any computer-session span: 12,708 world actions, 7,790 privileged (61.3%); these are the agent working from its SDK loop directly and are not chained here.

Tool mix (all sessions): mcp__village__computer_use 7,124, Read 4,686, mcp__village__bash 4,363, Bash 540, Edit 79, Grep 45, Write 24, mcp__village__request_google_sign_in 21, Glob 10, WebSearch 8, WebFetch 3

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P2 3,226, P3 166

**Subagent spawns (P4):** 0 across 0 sessions. Of the spawn instructions, 0 contain any constraint-like language (`village goal`, `do not`, `must not`, `never`, `only`), a crude proxy for whether the parent transmitted its constraints; median instruction length 0 characters.

## A. Computer-use sessions, all agents (2025-04-02 to 2026-09-19)

### Per session: actions n, privileged-class bash actions k

- sessions: 78,111
- chain length n: mean 31.1; median 40; p90 41; p99 44
- privileged-class actions k: mean 4.48; median 1; p90 15; p99 32
- privileged share of actions k/n: 0.144
- sessions with **no** privileged action (a declaration gate costs them nothing): 47.1%
- sessions with 3 or more: 38.5%

| per-action survival p | uniform tax: mean pⁿ | declaration gate: mean pᵏ |
|---|---|---|
| 0.99 | 0.738 | 0.958 |
| 0.95 | 0.267 | 0.839 |
| 0.9 | 0.120 | 0.749 |

Bash actions are 40.3% of all actions; GUI actions (click, type, scroll) are the rest and are not classified, so k is a floor.

| model family | sessions | mean n | mean k | share k=0 | k/n |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| claude | 28,997 | 31.3 | 4.51 | 48.9% | 0.144 |
| gpt/o | 22,705 | 27.1 | 3.60 | 47.3% | 0.133 |
| gemini | 15,745 | 35.5 | 2.47 | 62.8% | 0.070 |
| other | 10,664 | 32.8 | 9.22 | 19.0% | 0.281 |

Privileged classes (session-level counts): P2 334,099, P3 35,717, P4 13,160

## Reading

The uniform-tax column is what per-step friction would do to completion if each step survived with probability p: with real chain lengths it collapses quickly. The declaration-gate column is the same survival applied only at privileged-class actions, which is what the harness actually implements and what RESULTS.md found carries the effect. The gap between the two columns, and the share of sessions with k = 0, is the throughput argument for keying friction to a syntactic privileged class rather than to every step.
